item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit bfc2e069; the guard compares an imported value rule's target_path and target_index against reference rules via the existing _agrees predicate and records a conflict only when a reference rule sits on that same target and does not agree, with no existing test weakened.
item_verdicts.done_when: section 13's three clauses each hold at the reviewed head: a row on a hand-built target with a different source array is counted and listed with both arrays (test_conflicting_counts_a_target_whose_source_array_differs, plus the CLI test reading magnetics conflicting=1), a row on a target with no hand-built rule is not counted (test_a_target_without_a_hand_built_rule_is_not_conflicting), and an agreeing row is not counted (test_an_agreeing_row_is_not_conflicting); all green in review-head-arm.log.
item_verdicts.goal: read imas_ambix/data/handoff_score.py against plan section 13; _measure now returns a conflicting count and a conflicts list per IDS and structure row and total sums the count, printed by maps_cli.score_handoff_command as a new conflicting column - exactly the section's clause.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, one commit bfc2e069, the head gate and negative-control logs named, baseline_suite and after_suite recorded as null.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the review diff base=e9b69a99..head=bfc2e069 is exactly the five declared files; nothing outside scope changed.

justifications.durability: tests/data/test_handoff_score.py adds three tests exercising all three done-when clauses: test_conflicting_counts_a_target_whose_source_array_differs (a different-source-array row on a hand-built target is counted and listed with both arrays), test_a_target_without_a_hand_built_rule_is_not_conflicting, and test_an_agreeing_row_is_not_conflicting. An independently applied mutation removing the on-target guard (counting every non-agreeing imported row as conflicting) fails test_a_target_without_a_hand_built_rule_is_not_conflicting as 1 failed, 9 passed EXIT=1 (review-negative-control.log), reproducing the run's own negative-control.log; the printed-table column is covered by tests/test_maps_cli.py::test_score_handoff_prints_a_conflicting_column, which asserts the header order and the magnetics/TOTAL conflicting cells. The guard is shown to fire, not merely to pass.
justifications.evidence: Re-measured independently: head arm at bfc2e069 (tests/data/test_handoff_score.py + tests/test_maps_cli.py) 48 passed EXIT=0 (review-head-arm.log, module.__file__ under the bfc2e069 archive); base arm at e9b69a99 (same files) 44 passed EXIT=0 (review-base-arm.log). The run's own head-gate.log was red with 2 draft_signals failures reading the shared maps bundle, unrelated to this change and outside scope; no new failing id is added (added_failure_count 0). The run's own negative control and my independent one both redden the no-hand-built-rule test with EXIT=1. Marker check: 'conflicting' occurs 2 times in the head tree's handoff_score.py and 0 times in the base tree's, confirming the change landed.
justifications.fit: imas_ambix/data/handoff_score.py extends the existing _measure dict shape with two adjacent keys and reuses the module's own _agrees predicate and Counter idiom; maps_cli.py edits only the header string and the row f-string column order. No new module, dependency or name was introduced.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_ambix/data/handoff_score.py:117-140 adds conflicting and conflicts to the per-row dict returned for both by_ids and by_structure, and score_handoff totals conflicting across IDSs; each conflicts entry carries target_path, target_index, imported_source_array and the sorted hand_built_source_arrays, so each conflict is listed with both source arrays as section 13 requires, and the printed table shows the count. This covers the MMSYS curUFPdisr/curLFPdisr case the section motivates: an imported row binding a coil target by a different source array now reads as a conflict.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses _agrees as the agreement authority rather than re-deriving a comparison, keeps the single per-row dict returned by _measure, and adds no parallel scorer; maps_cli reuses row['conflicting'] directly.
justifications.scope_discipline: the review diff base=e9b69a99..head=bfc2e069 is exactly five files - imas_ambix/data/handoff_score.py, imas_ambix/maps_cli.py, tests/data/test_handoff_score.py, tests/test_maps_cli.py, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-tokamap-from-generated-maps/handoff-score-conflicts.html - all inside the node's declared write paths; no file outside scope changed and no existing test was weakened.
